title: The Prayer of the Just and the Glory of God
english: Are they undermining the words, those enemies of the truth, intending to speak and to shout in order to deceive, to test and to provoke, having such a purpose?

But also, since Babylon is interpreted as a symbol of that which brings shame upon those doing evil, accordingly the king of this [Babylon] will be struck and killed along with the king of Zion among the Amorites, so that the land may be given to Israel. They ruled it badly through sophistry and through a wearying life, meddling in the nature of things and appearing to rule it; but their interpreted land being taken away, it is given as a possession to Israel to inherit it, becoming a true servant of the cause of all things. (Ps 135:23-24: And when we were brought low through misfortune, he remembers us and redeems us.)

Let my confession be upon your mercy and your truth, since, having been often shown mercy and having seen the truth which was enlightened in me by you, I was rescued from all evil and from its related deception, you providing remission of sins through your mercy and keeping me from all wandering through your truth. (Ps 137:2: Let my confession be upon your mercy and your truth...)

But since you have magnified the word given to me by you, depending on it through your presence as if it were your own wealth, I will worship toward your holy temple and I will confess your name, giving thanks that your word is being magnified in me; for then it is magnified in me, and since I am progressing by it, I hasten toward its perfection. (Ps 137:2d: Another scripture is brought forth saying, 'That you have magnified your holy name above all.')

When is this fulfilled? When every knee shall bow in the name of Jesus, both heavenly and earthly and under the earth, every tongue confessing what the Lord Jesus Christ is, to the glory of God the Father, announcing to his brothers who have come to be the Son's likeness the greatness of the Father's presence; for he has not come alone in the name of the Father, so that the holy name of God might be magnified above all. We learn to say in prayer, 'Hallowed be your name.' But just as the hallowed name of God does not become holy from something profane, but is shown to be such, it is not magnified by increase as...

To become great from something small, but with his greatness being made manifest. The one who prays unceasingly and performs this by spirit and mind: 'I will pray, saying, by spirit, and I will pray also by the mind,' having God as a listener on each day, concerning whom it has been written, 'and the ears of the Lord are toward the righteous, and to their supplication' (Ps 137:3). For one possesses God as a guardian who does not delay nor despise him, but watches over him in his provident power.

Because of setting the mind on earthly things and seeking the lower and temporal things, making a profit, the peoples of the earth—about which the prophecy says here—the reason for wanting all the words of your mouth that you spoke in the law and in the prophets concerning their calling is this: for even if they are not hearers of your oracles, it is not by their power that their faith was foreknown. Therefore also I desire to reach them with diligent and musical recitation in your ways, namely, the Scriptures, so that one traveling through them by continuous study and reading might diligently proclaim the meanings from them. And if someone speaks of the virtuous ways of the Lord, and someone traveling diligently through these [ways] sings triumphal hymns against the wickedness that of old was working in them; if someone diligently speaks the word of virtuous activity concerning each of the ways of the Lord, having sent forth a diligent voice through the actions according to them.

All these things shall be made perfect, since also the glory of the Lord which performs these things is great, concerning which it is said toward Jerusalem: 'And the glory of the Lord has risen upon you, and all flesh shall see the salvation of our God' (Ps 137:4-5), since the glory of the Lord shall be seen. And who then is this, the savior, being a radiance of the glory of God and a character of his substance? It is brought here instead of 'Peoples' as 'Kings': 'Let all the kings of the earth confess to you, O Lord' (Ps 137:6). And both expressions have harmony with the concept of being called to reign, the peoples confessing to the Lord being set as a royal priesthood and a holy nation (Ex 19:6); and toward some of them it is written, 'And you have reigned, so that we also may reign with you' (2 Sam 5:11).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Inaccessibility of Divine Wisdom
english: Not only concerning the Father, but also concerning the Son, these things are to be spoken, since He holds all things made through Him and they exist in Him, and above all things He is. Thus also the almighty rule is ordered upon Him, as in the prophet Zechariah (Zech 4:6). Even if the High Lord sees someone among the lowly, He is high to the heavenly and is of a nature that has ascended far above, but He does not only know these things from a distance as being far from Him by a change of existence.

In this way, the apostolic word is like it: 'Beloved, do not avenge yourselves, but give place to the wrath; for it is written, Vengeance is mine, I will repay, says the Lord' (Rom 12:19; Deut 32:35).' That is, do not hand us men over to invisible enemies intent on killing us. By which I press forward, striving to reach the prize of the high calling (Ps 138:7).

And it is nothing wonderful if He knew all things concerning me, He says (Ps 138:5); for knowing all things, He does not merely observe them, but also the beginnings and the ends of them, and the causes by which they came to be, and what will be about them after the cosmic variety. Having formed me with knowledge of all things, You placed Your hand upon me, which is said first. Having placed Your hand upon me, and having formed me from dust and clay as a man, it is as if a wise one said: 'Your hands made me and formed me,' and likewise, 'Remember what clay You formed me from.'

And it is also not so; having formed me, You were not satisfied with having made me, but You also placed Your hand upon me in order to improve and guard me and to lift me up by it. Therefore, let him who understands this gift and advises others be careful, saying, 'Humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, so that He may lift you up in due time' (1 Pet 5:6), so that, being secured by it, you may not have any insolence or scheme occur. For no one snatches from the hand of the Father; for the invisible enemies only tear apart those who have been cast away from it. Having understood how You have knowledge of all things, I have come to a marvel. But even if, having understood, I marveled at Your knowledge, it is not that my will understands it on my behalf, having been made [by You].

It has been strengthened so that I might not be able to reach it. This is consistent with what is in Ecclesiastes: 'I said, I will be wise, but wisdom has departed from me, and it was made far from me, beyond my reach; who can find it?' (Eccl 8:17). And also Paul left the same voices, saying: 'O the depth of the riches and the wisdom and the knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments and untraceable are his ways!' (Rom 11:33). And he himself says this, since he is not able to reach the knowledge of God having been strengthened beyond him.

It is also possible for that which is near me to show that your wisdom, which is wonderful, was not revealed to me, because once it is strengthened, I will no longer be able to oppose or strike at it. And if even concerning the knowledge of God, the saint himself has words about it as one who is grasping it, discussing the things set forth, having visited it. Having theologized about the things concerning the foreknowledge of God, that He is, and has the knowledge and understanding of all things, he moves on to say that He is everywhere.

He indeed says toward the one being theologized about: 'If your spirit has filled the inhabited world, where shall I go from it? But since your face also observes and looks upon all things, where shall I flee from it? For ascending into heaven, with you present, I receive a vision; if I become in Hades, I see you present' (Ps 138:7-12). And if in heaven and in Hades your presence is known, and in the intermediate places it is evident that you are there; 'Do I not fill the heaven and the earth?' says the Lord, as the prophet says (Jer 23:24). But also in the sea itself, he manifests himself to those seeking him, as the following word presents.

Therefore also, one of the theologians says to one of those listening: 'And he shall know by intellect what God is in the heaven above and on the earth below, and there is nothing besides Him.' But He presents Himself everywhere, not locally dwelling, but creatively and providentially entering into all things. For he says concerning the only-begotten Word that all things consist in him; and if all things have been established in him, nothing of those established in him is left out from him. And we learn also from the things set forth the theologized Trinity. For the Holy Spirit, the Spirit of God, has often been demonstrated to be a person, his only-begotten Son being an image of him.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Illumination of the Night
english: It is said to be the being of the invisible God, and also the character of his own subsistence. From this we learn that the Spirit of God is not a creature, but is joined to the God himself and to his person. For it has often been shown that He is never with the creation, but always united to the Father and the Son. Only this is presented as a contrast: that I must pass locally and ascend, while it is your case to be present and to be established there, in having made him and turning him, and also to descend into the sea similarly passing, by your presence of providence there.

Therefore, God is not in a place; for if he is everywhere, not passing from one place to another, nor being limited by each one, nor being circumscribed by all the places, it is evident that by a creative and providential presence he moves through all, upon all, through all, and exists in all, according to apostolic philosophy (Ps 138:9-10). 'I searched,' he says, 'whether by using the wings of thought I might have gone far beyond the sea and the ocean's end, whether I would be able to go from your spirit and flee from your face, and there also to have seen your active and providential hand, and that very right hand of yours surpassing, working; as this very thing, that to have dwelt with me, would be established for me in a predicted sequence at the ends of the sea, your hand guiding me and holding me with your right hand.' For even if the ocean is boundless, yet even the worlds with it are driven through by the commands of the Lord; for all things having been made toward him, whatever they ever are, are straightened for me by the commands of his own providence (Ps 138:11-14a).

Since being enlightened by the knowledge of the Lord, I have become in the morning at the beginning of the day, I meditated on glories with the intellectual wings through which every rational nature is lifted up to be far off and beyond the ocean, he also knew this: that he could not go from the spirit of God or its guidance, to seek another way, by which to go from the spirit and flee from the face of God who is, lest perhaps by darkness...

I will be able to speak this having happened. Therefore I say, 'Alas, darkness will tread upon me,' that is, it will cover me. For just as the floor that is being trodden upon is hidden, not being hidden underneath, if the darkness happens to tread much around me and upon me.

If indeed the glory is a luxury regarding the attainment of what is labored for, immediately even the night and the gloomy darkness is illumination, nothing of that darkness being darkened by God illuminating it just as also all other things. For among us, those using the distinction see the difference between night and day, and those seeing in the day, but in the night they neither see nor are seen; but with God, the night is illuminated as the day, seizing for himself those in darkness and night as those in light and day, since the night is illuminated as the day by God himself.

The righteous man applies all these things to himself, having intended to teach those having wrong opinion about God that it is not possible to flee from God. For are those thinking these things about God, to say even the God himself, 'Will someone not be hidden in secret places, and I will not find him?' (Ps 139:12), for God is approaching all, and I am not God from a distance. Cain has become a father of this ill-reputation, having said to God, 'If you cast me out from the face of the earth today, and from your face I will be hidden' (Gen 4:14).

And another, through surpassing foolishness, sinning in a dim and gloomy place and night, says, 'Darkness covers me from every side, and the walls cover me; who sees me?' (Eccl 10:3); 'The Most High will not remember my sins' (Ps 139:12), saying only once, 'Since in darkness and in the midst of the gloom I sin, with no one present, I elude everyone, and even the Most High would not know my sins.'

But stop, for if someone becomes further than the word concerning darkness, he will be able to behold mysteries, if the division of the things being said is such: 'Will I indeed be able to flee from God, having become evil and trivial, as to become under the darkness and to be trodden upon by it?' But having thought this, he immediately knew that even the night is illuminated in the day, that is, in the luxury of the rational animal; for illumination from virtue and knowledge is truly and appropriately a luxury for the rational animal.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
